newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gas oil falls $4.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gas oil falls $4.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Friday, traders said.
Gasoline was broadly steady by the end of business on Friday having faced a bumpy ride in line with crude and NYMEX gasoline's fortunes.
Eurograde material was assessed around a steady $221-224 cif, but no physical trade was heard. Demand from the U.S was expected to draw barrels transatlantic next week.
Naphtha was thinly offered. Dealers said barrels were around but most appeared to have homes or owners had specific plans for them.
Algerian and Egyptian product were pegged notionally around cif high quotes +$3.
Gas oil slid $4 a tonne on easier futures as temperatures started to climb back to normal after a cold snap.
Russian 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil volumes were heavy, absorbing most current demand, and premiums were steady to slightly firmer ahead of a busy programme of loadings in the next week.
At least four Russian cargoes changed hands, one going for high cif Med quotes +$1.75 basis Genoa for January 18/20. A low sulphur diesel cargo was done at cif Med mean quotes flat.
High sulphur fuel oil was steady to weaker despite good bunker demand, traders said.

A single trader was thought to have won a three-cargo bunker tender for Malta in January, February and March, but the price was not known. Another trader was heard to have won a tender for two 50,000 tonne cargoes of good bunker quality material to be delivered to Syria in the second half of January. Again, the price was not known.
Traders were also eyeing a Turkish tender for 45,000-50,000 tonnes of low sulphur cracked fuel oil, for delivery at the end of January.
The sale of some 80,000 tonnes of Italian material into Romania has taken out some of January's length.
Low sulphur fuel oil was assessed steady to firmer.
